title: Scheduled tasks & background jobs in your app
content:
<Callout type="warning" title="In-process schedulers will fail under scale-to-zero">
If your app uses an in-process scheduler—APScheduler, Celery beat, Python's `threading.Timer`, or similar—those tasks **will not run** when your container scales to zero. On lower tiers that scale to zero after inactivity, scheduled jobs can silently die, causing missed runs and data inconsistency.
</Callout>

## Why in-process schedulers break

Emergent's platform automatically scales your container to zero replicas when no HTTP requests arrive for a period. This saves resources and keeps costs predictable. When the next request arrives, a fresh container spins up.

**The problem:** schedulers like APScheduler and Celery beat run inside your application process. When the container stops, the scheduler stops. When a new container starts later, it has no memory of what was scheduled—missed intervals are lost, and one-time jobs scheduled for a past timestamp will never fire.

Common symptoms:

- Daily data exports never run
- Periodic cleanup tasks accumulate stale records
- Notification reminders are skipped
- Background aggregations drift out of sync

## Recommended patterns

Choose one of the following approaches based on your tier and workload:

<Tabs>
<Tab title="External cron (recommended for most apps)">
**Use an external service to trigger an HTTP endpoint** on your app at the desired interval. This works on every tier, including those that scale to zero.

<Steps>
<Step title="Create a task endpoint">
Add a route that performs the scheduled work:

```python
@app.post("/tasks/daily-cleanup")
def daily_cleanup(request):
    # Validate secret header to prevent abuse
    if request.headers.get("X-Cron-Secret") != os.getenv("CRON_SECRET"):
        return {"error": "Unauthorized"}, 401
    
    # Perform the task
    db.stale_records.delete_many({"created_at": {"$lt": cutoff_date}})
    return {"status": "ok"}
```
</Step>

<Step title="Protect the endpoint">
Set a secret environment variable (`CRON_SECRET`) and check it in the handler to prevent public abuse.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure an external trigger">
Use a service like:

- [GitHub Actions scheduled workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#schedule) (free, YAML cron syntax)
- [EasyCron](https://www.easycron.com/) or [cron-job.org](https://cron-job.org) (free tiers available)
- Cloud provider cron (AWS EventBridge, GCP Cloud Scheduler, Azure Logic Apps)

Point the trigger at `https://your-app.emergent.run/tasks/daily-cleanup` with the secret header.
</Step>
</Steps>

**Pros:**  
• Works on all tiers  
• Reliable timing even when app is idle  
• Simple to test and debug

**Cons:**  
• Requires external dependency  
• Adds a small coordination overhead
</Tab>

<Tab title="Always-on tier">
If you upgrade to a tier that **does not scale to zero**, in-process schedulers will work reliably because at least one container is always running.

Check your plan's scaling behavior in the [workspace settings](/a-tour-of-the-workspace#deployment-tiers). Tiers labeled "always-on" or "minimum 1 replica" maintain scheduler state.

**Pros:**  
• Familiar libraries (APScheduler, Celery beat)  
• No external coordination needed

**Cons:**  
• Higher cost (containers run 24/7)  
• Still at risk if your single replica crashes and restarts
</Tab>

<Tab title="Decoupled async workers">
For complex task graphs or high-volume queues, use a **dedicated message broker and worker process**:

- **Broker:** Redis (via [Upstash](https://upstash.com/) or self-hosted) or a managed queue (AWS SQS, GCP Pub/Sub)
- **Worker framework:** Celery with Redis backend, or RQ (Python)
- **Scheduler:** External cron pushes messages to the broker; workers consume them

This pattern decouples scheduling from execution and scales workers independently of your web tier.

**Pros:**  
• Resilient to web-tier restarts  
• Scales task processing independently  
• Supports retries, task prioritization, and parallel execution

**Cons:**  
• More infrastructure to manage  
• Additional cost for broker and worker containers
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Migration checklist

If you currently rely on an in-process scheduler:

<Steps>
<Step title="Audit scheduled tasks">
List every cron, interval, or delayed job currently running in-process.
</Step>

<Step title="Choose a pattern">
External cron for simple periodic tasks; always-on tier or decoupled workers for complex workloads.
</Step>

<Step title="Refactor to HTTP endpoints">
Move task logic into routes protected by a secret header.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure external triggers">
Set up GitHub Actions workflows, cloud cron jobs, or a third-party service.
</Step>

<Step title="Remove in-process scheduler">
Delete APScheduler, Celery beat, or threading logic from your app startup to avoid confusion.
</Step>

<Step title="Test end-to-end">
Trigger the endpoint manually, then wait for the scheduled run to confirm the external service is working.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Example: migrating APScheduler to external cron

**Before (in-process, fails on scale-to-zero):**

```python
from apscheduler.schedulers.background import BackgroundScheduler

scheduler = BackgroundScheduler()
scheduler.add_job(cleanup_stale_records, 'cron', hour=2)
scheduler.start()
```

**After (external cron triggers HTTP endpoint):**

```python
@app.post("/tasks/cleanup")
def cleanup_task(request):
    if request.headers.get("X-Cron-Secret") != os.getenv("CRON_SECRET"):
        return {"error": "Unauthorized"}, 401
    
    cleanup_stale_records()
    return {"status": "completed"}
```

**GitHub Actions workflow** (`.github/workflows/daily-cleanup.yml`):

```yaml
name: Daily cleanup
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'  # 02:00 UTC daily
jobs:
  trigger:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Call cleanup endpoint
        run: |
          curl -X POST https://your-app.emergent.run/tasks/cleanup \
            -H "X-Cron-Secret: ${{ secrets.CRON_SECRET }}"
```

<Tip>
Store `CRON_SECRET` in your repository's GitHub secrets and mirror it as an environment variable in your Emergent [workspace settings](/a-tour-of-the-workspace#environment-variables).
</Tip>
